t: G25 Axiomatic Repository: Content-Addressed Archive — Simple
name: G25 Axiomatic Repository: Content-Addressed Archive — Simple
title: G25 Axiomatic Repository: Content-Addressed Archive — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] The archive where the address IS the hash: store a blob, name it by its SHA-256, and integrity verification becomes a recompute-and-compare. The collision odds for a billion blobs are computed below — small enough to bet the archive on.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Collision odds, 1B blobs in 256-bit space = 4.318e-60 probability. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: The Master Axiomatic Repository (G25) – Quantifying the Systemic Refuge Constant (SRC)
real_world_basis: Content-addressed storage (git, IPFS, CAS archives) is the real, standard design this implements.
signature_version: Signature version: the SRC archive — the chapter's Systemic Refuge Constant as the durability target (nines of durability), with the 'absolute refuge' framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: pick the hash, build the ingest pipeline, and verify on every read.
math_note: Collision odds, 1B blobs in 256-bit space: 4.318e-60 probability [verified]; Dedup addresses for 1M identical blobs: 1 addresses [verified]

math_check.label: Dedup addresses for 1M identical blobs
math_check.note: corrected 2026-10-19: formula was d/dx[x^3], unrelated to the claim

safety: No hazard; the failure mode is silent bit-rot — verify, don't assume.
how_it_works: Hash each blob on ingest, store under the digest, and verify by rehashing on read. Deduplication falls out free: identical blobs share one address. The demo computes the birthday collision bound.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact

t: G25 Axiomatic Repository: RAID Parity Budget — Simple
name: G25 Axiomatic Repository: RAID Parity Budget — Simple
title: G25 Axiomatic Repository: RAID Parity Budget — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] The redundancy arithmetic: RAID-6 survives any two disk failures with 2 parity disks per stripe; erasure coding generalizes it to m parity fragments per n data. The budget is usable capacity = raw × n/(n+m), computed before buying disks.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Usable TB from 120 TB raw, 8+2 erasure = 96.0 TB. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
